[{"node":"loopar_printing_menu_content","element":"menu_content","data":{"key":"loopar_printing_menu_content","id":"loopar_printing_menu_content","name":"loopar_printing_menu_content"},"elements":[{"node":"printing-overview","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Overview","key":"printing-overview","id":"printing-overview","name":"printing-overview","value":"# Printing & Signatures Every document entity can be printed: `/desk//print?name=` (the **Print** button of the form) opens a printable sheet the user prints or saves as PDF from the browser. The sheet is always white paper with the organization's letterhead, whatever the Desk theme. Which layout is used, in order: | Priority | Layout | How you get it | |----------|--------|----------------| | 1 | A **Print Format** (the one requested with `&format=`, else the entity's default) | Designed in the Print Format Builder | | 2 | The app's **`client/-print.jsx`** | Written in React | | 3 | The **automatic format** | Built from the entity's own form structure | `&format=standard` forces 2 or 3. When an entity has several formats, the print view offers a picker, plus the paper size (Letter, Legal, A4) and orientation, remembered per browser. `print` is a permission of its own: grant it per role like any other action. "}},{"node":"printing-company","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Company & Letterheads","key":"printing-company","id":"printing-company","name":"printing-company","value":"## Company & Letterheads ### Company **Company** (a single record, seeded by the install wizard) is the organization's identity: name, legal name, tax id (with its own label, e.g. *VAT*, *EIN*), contact details, address, logos, brand colors, currency, time zone and date format. Prints, letterheads and themes read it — enter it once. Server code reads it with `getCompany()`: ```javascript import { getCompany } from "loopar"; const company = await getCompany(); company.company_name; company.currency; company.address_text; ``` ### Letterheads A **Letterhead** adds what changes between documents on top of the Company: a **tagline** and a **footer** (bank details, legal text…). Mark one as **Default**; a Print Format can pick another one. The printed letterhead = Company identity (logo, names, tax id, address, phone, email, website) + the letterhead's tagline and footer. "}},{"node":"printing-formats","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Print Formats","key":"printing-formats","id":"printing-formats","name":"printing-formats","value":"## Print Formats Create one with **Print Format Builder** → **New**: | Field | Description | |-------|-------------| | **Name** / **Module** | The format and the app module it ships with | | **Entity to print** | The entity it prints — **Load entity** brings its fields into the designer | | **Letterhead** | Empty = the default letterhead | | **Paper size** / **Orientation** | Letter, Legal, A4 · Portrait, Landscape | | **Default for the entity** | Use it when no format is requested | | **Disabled** | Hide it from the picker | The **Print Designer** offers layout and content elements plus the **print** group, which read the record being printed: | Element | Prints | |---------|--------| | `letterhead` | The letterhead (Company + tagline) | | `doc_header` | Document title, name and state | | `doc_field` | One field, with its label, formatted (dates, money, selects show their title) | | `doc_table` | A child table — choose the columns, or leave empty for its list columns | | `doc_section` | A titled block to group fields | | `doc_body` | Every field of the form, in its own layout | | `page_break` | Start a new page | Outside a print (in the designer) these elements show placeholders. **Preview** a format on real data: `/desk//view?name=` (the latest record when no name is given). It needs `print` with scope `all` on the entity. Formats are files of the app, so they ship and update with it. "}},{"node":"printing-react","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Print in React","key":"printing-react","id":"printing-react","name":"printing-react","value":"## Print in React When a layout needs logic — totals computed on the fly, different blocks per status — write `client/-print.jsx`: ```jsx import { useDocument } from "@loopar/document"; import { PrintLayout, LetterheadBlock, LetterheadFooter, formatPrintValue } from "@loopar/print"; export default function InvoicePrint() { const { Document } = useDocument(); const doc = Document?.data || {}; return (

Invoice {doc.name}

Total: {formatPrintValue("money", doc.total)}

 ); } ``` `PrintLayout` provides the paper, the toolbar and the record; use the `--lp-*` paper palette for colors, never theme colors, so the sheet stays printable in dark mode. A designed Print Format still wins over this file when one is the default. "}},{"node":"printing-signatures","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"E-signatures","key":"printing-signatures","id":"printing-signatures","name":"printing-signatures","value":"## Electronic Signatures Any record can ask someone **outside the system** — a client, a supplier — to sign a document through a link, without an account. ```javascript import { loopar } from "loopar"; // The model class of the core "Signature Request" entity const SignatureRequest = (await loopar.newDocument("Signature Request")).constructor; const { request, url, emailed } = await SignatureRequest.issue({ document: "Service Agreement", // source entity documentName: "SA-0001", // source record title: "Service Agreement", html, // exactly what the signer will read signerName: "Jane Doe", signerEmail: "jane@example.com", days: 30, // link lifetime (default 30) message: "Please review and sign.", }); ``` A new request replaces any pending one of the same record. `emailed` is `false` when the email couldn't be sent — show `url` to the user so they can share it another way. The signer gets an email with the link (sent with the tenant's email settings). The signing page shows the document; the signer types their name and title, accepts, and signs — or declines with a reason. ### Evidence Each **Signature Request** keeps: the exact HTML shown and its **SHA-256**, typed name and title, consent, sent / first viewed / signed times, IP address and browser. Status: `Pending`, `Signed`, `Declined`, `Expired`, `Revoked`. ### Hooks on the source record ```javascript export default class ServiceAgreement extends BaseDocument { async onSignatureSigned(request) { /* e.g. run a workflow transition */ } async onSignatureDeclined(request) { /* notify the owner */ } } ``` ### Links and setup - Only a **hash** of the link token is stored. **Resend** issues a new link and invalidates the previous one; **Revoke** cancels the request. - The website needs a page for signing: add a menu row (*router only*) with page **Document Signing** and a link such as `sign`. "}}]}]
